html:
Multichannel convolution
Guided demo
Click a blue filter stack (or a pink output sheet) to isolate one filter → one output channel. Drag the figure to ease out the oblique shear and see the true 3D stacking.
⚠ Figure failed to load

plan.contextChunk: This figure lays out a multichannel convolution as one symbolic equation joining three groups of tensors drawn in offset perspective. On the left, under the bold label w, sit two stacks of light blue square grids, each three sheets deep; a tall brace at the far left reads C_out filters and spans both stacks, a small brace above the upper stack reads C_in, and braces along the right side and the bottom edge of the lower stack each read K for the filter's two spatial extents. A star operator separates the filter bank from the middle group, labeled x_in, a much larger pink grid also drawn as three offset sheets, with a brace above reading C_in and a brace beneath its width reading M. An equals sign leads to the right-hand group, labeled x_out, a single pink grid whose upper brace reads C_out and whose right-hand brace reads N. Color keeps the learned parameters distinct from the data, and the braces let the reader match dimensions straight across the operator: the filter bank's depth agrees with the input's C_in, while the number of filters becomes the output's C_out. The drawing spells out shape bookkeeping that is easy to lose track of in symbols alone.

elements: Left group under bold label 'w': two stacks of light-blue square grids, each stack made of 3 offset same-size sheets (depth = C_in), each sheet a K×K cell grid with black cell borders
Tall curly brace at far left spanning both blue stacks, rotated label 'C_out filters'
Small curly brace above the upper blue stack pointing along its receding diagonal, label 'C_in'
Curly brace on the right edge of the lower blue stack, label 'K' (vertical filter extent)
Curly brace under the bottom edge of the lower blue stack, label 'K' (horizontal filter extent)
Star convolution operator '⋆' between the filter bank and the input, at mid-height
Middle group under bold label 'x_in': one pink stack of 3 offset same-size sheets (depth = C_in), each sheet an M×M cell grid (M = 8) with black cell borders
Curly brace above the pink input stack, label 'C_in'
Curly brace under the front pink input sheet's bottom edge, label 'M'
Equals sign '=' between input and output groups
Right group under bold label 'x_out': pink stack of sheets, one sheet per output channel (C_out), each sheet an N×N cell grid with N = M − K + 1
Curly brace above the pink output stack, label 'C_out'
Curly brace on the right edge of the front output sheet, label 'N'
Bold italic labels 'w', 'x_in', 'x_out' centered above their groups

interactions.teaches: Each blue filter in the bank produces exactly one pink output channel, so C_out is set by how many filters you stack, not by the input depth.
interactions.label: C_out (number of filters)

interactions.teaches: K is the filter's spatial footprint, independent of the input width M; growing K enlarges the highlighted receptive patch on x_in and shrinks the output to N = M − K + 1.
interactions.label: K (kernel size)

interactions.teaches: Clicking one filter stack dims the others and highlights only its output sheet, making the one-filter-to-one-output-channel mapping explicit; the filter's C_in sheets align one-to-one with the input's C_in sheets.
interactions.label: Select a filter

demo_steps.title: Two filters, 3×3
demo_steps.narration: The bank holds C_out = 2 filters, each three sheets deep to match the input's C_in = 3 channels. The output stack has exactly two pink sheets.

demo_steps.title: Add filters
demo_steps.narration: Raising C_out to 4 adds blue filter stacks on the left and, sheet for sheet, pink channels on the right — the input is untouched.

demo_steps.title: Grow the kernel
demo_steps.narration: With K = 5 each filter's footprint widens, the highlighted patch on x_in covers 5×5 cells, and the output shrinks to N = M − K + 1 = 4 while C_out stays fixed.

demo_steps.title: Shrink to 1×1
demo_steps.narration: At K = 1 the filter is a single cell per channel, the output is as wide as the input (N = M), showing that spatial extent K and input width M are separate quantities.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Oblique: +X screen-right, +Y screen-up, +Z the receding diagonal drawn up-and-right; sheets are flat X×Y quads of thickness 0.04 in Z, successive sheets offset by (+0.22, +0.22) on screen along the diagonal. Cell sizes follow the source, where filter cells are drawn larger than data cells: filter cell 0.42 units, input/output cell 0.30 units. Blue filter sheet = (K·0.42) × (K·0.42) × 0.04, default K=3 → 1.26×1.26. Each filter stack has exactly C_in = 3 sheets. Pink input sheet = (8·0.30)×(8·0.30) = 2.4×2.4, M = 8 cells, 3 sheets (C_in = 3). Pink output sheet = (N·0.30)×(N·0.30) with N = M − K + 1 (K=3 → N=6 → 1.8×1.8); number of output sheets equals the C_out slider, drawn with the same 0.22 diagonal offset. Layout along X (screen-left to right, all groups vertically centered near y=0): blue filter stacks centered at x = −4.2, stacked vertically with the upper stack centered at y = +1.1 and the lower at y = −1.1 (spacing 2.2, shrinking toward center if C_out < 2 and extending outward symmetrically if C_out > 2, total vertical span capped at ~5 units); '⋆' glyph at (−2.5, 0); pink input stack centered at (−0.7, 0); '=' glyph at (1.4, 0); pink output stack centered at (3.4, 0). Labels 'w' at (−4.2, 2.9), 'x_in' at (−0.7, 2.0), 'x_out' at (3.4, 1.7), all bold serif black. Braces: tall left brace at x = −5.6 spanning y = −2.4…+2.4 with rotated label 'C_out filters' at x = −6.1; small C_in brace above the top blue stack following the diagonal; 'K' brace on the right edge of the lower blue stack and 'K' brace under its bottom edge; 'C_in' brace above the pink input stack along its diagonal; 'M' brace under the front input sheet at y ≈ −1.6; 'C_out' brace above the output stack; 'N' brace at the right edge of the front output sheet. Colors: blue fill #CFE4F3, pink fill #F8DAD6, all cell lines and outlines black #000000 at ~1.5px, labels black. Selected/highlighted state: keep full saturation and add a gold outline #E0A526; deselected items fade to 25% opacity. Receptive patch on x_in: K×K cells highlighted in a deeper pink #F0B2AB at the top-left of the front input sheet.
interactionPlan.notes: Render with an OrthographicCamera and build the oblique look by shearing each sheet group in screen space (or place sheets on parallel XY planes and offset each by a constant screen-space vector) — no perspective foreshortening, all sheets in a stack identical in size. Draw each grid as a filled PlaneGeometry plus LineSegments for the cell lattice so line width stays crisp; regenerate lattices when K or M changes. Braces are Shape/ExtrudeGeometry-free: build them as 2D CatmullRom curves in an overlaid SVG/CSS layer or as Line objects on the camera-facing plane, scaled to the current stack extents so they track the sliders. Labels ('w', 'x_in', 'x_out', C_in, C_out, K, M, N, ⋆, =) as CSS2DRenderer HTML with MathJax-style italic serif. On slider change, animate sheet add/remove with a short opacity+offset tween so the learner sees which sheet appeared. Painter ordering: draw the far-most sheet of each stack first (renderOrder by Z) to preserve the overlap illusion.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for C_out filters; the learner increases or decreases the number of blue filter stacks, the pink output stack gains or loses matching sheets, and the one-filter-to-one-output-channel relationship becomes explicit.
- Slider for kernel size K; the learner changes the blue filter grid footprint, the highlighted receptive patch on x_in grows or shrinks, and the distinction between spatial filter extent K and input width M becomes clear.

discrepancies: A deeper-pink K×K receptive patch is drawn on the front input sheet; no such highlight exists in the source figure (added pedagogical element, minor clutter).
Overall figure scale is small in the viewport — the source fills the frame, whereas the generated stacks occupy only the central third, making grid lines and braces less legible at default zoom.
The output stack's channel-offset (and the C_out brace at its top-right) is tighter/smaller than in the source, so the x_out block reads as noticeably smaller relative to x_in than in the original.
Blue filter sheets' back layers show less distinct lattice/outline separation than the crisply outlined stacked squares in the source.
evaluation.notes: Very faithful oblique reconstruction of the multichannel convolution figure with correct stacked-sheet geometry, braces, operators and all key labels, plus genuinely useful C_out/K sliders, click-to-isolate selection and a guided 4-step demo; main weaknesses are the added receptive-patch highlight not in the source and a somewhat small on-canvas scale/label size.

feedback.rationale: Concept, geometry, labels and interactivity all score high with no action items and only minor cosmetic nits, so further iteration isn't warranted.
